children: , the advanced-lithography equipment powerhouse, is weighing a major production jump as AI-driven chip demand keeps pushing the limits of its supply chain, according to Reuters. JPMorgan analysts said after meeting the company's finance chief that ASML has studied a 2028 production ceiling above 110 extreme-ultraviolet lithography systems. U.S. shares climbed approximately 1.4% to $1,613.985, putting investors squarely back on the question of how quickly ASML can turn extraordinary demand into actual machine deliveries.

The numbers show how aggressive that expansion could become. ASML is already nearly sold out for 2027 and says it can manufacture at least 80 EUV systems that year. Moving beyond 110 machines would represent capacity at least 37.5% above that stated minimum. But ASML cannot scale alone. Its highly specialized suppliers must expand with it, making the broader semiconductor-equipment supply chain just as important as customer demand when investors think about the company's next leg of growth.

ASML already generated $9.33 billion in second-quarter sales, with a 54% gross margin and $2.92 billion in net income. The valuation picture shows just how much optimism is already embedded in the stock: at $1,613.985, the shares sit 27.67% above the $1.26K GF Value estimate. That premium raises the execution bar. AI demand can keep filling ASML's order book, but the bigger challenge now is whether the company and its suppliers can add capacity fast enough without sacrificing delivery discipline or margins.

title: ASML Gains 1.4% as EUV Capacity Chases a 110-Tool Threshold
